content.title: About
content.content: An egg omelet or scrambled eggs with meat is a dish made from beaten eggs, diced cooked meat (commonly ham, chicken or beef) and a splash of milk or cream. Eggs provide a complete protein source, while the meat adds extra protein, iron and flavor.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Meat‑filled omelets are a popular breakfast in Eastern Europe and many Asian countries.
The classic Russian version – “omelet po‑domashnemu” – includes ham and fresh herbs.
Eggs are one of the most affordable natural sources of vitamin D.
Meat in the omelet enhances iron absorption from the eggs thanks to heme iron.
Cooking over medium heat keeps the eggs tender and prevents the meat from drying out.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: Combined eggs and meat deliver a high amount of complete protein essential for muscle growth and repair.

items.title: B‑vitamin complex
items.content: Both ingredients supply B2, B6 and B12, supporting energy metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Iron source
items.content: Heme iron from meat is readily absorbed, helping to prevent anemia.

items.title: Beneficial fats
items.content: A modest amount of mono‑ and polyunsaturated fats from eggs and lean meat supports heart health.

items.title: Eye health
items.content: Lutein and zeaxanthin in the yolk protect the eyes from age‑related degeneration.

items.title: Egg allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to egg white proteins.

items.title: Cholesterol content
items.content: Egg yolks contain cholesterol; people with high cholesterol should consume in moderation.

items.title: Sodium in processed meat
items.content: Deli meats and ham can be high in salt, increasing hypertension risk if eaten excessively.

items.title: Food‑borne infection risk
items.content: Undercooked eggs may harbor Salmonella; cook until the whites are fully set.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the omelet hot, often garnished with herbs, tomatoes or whole‑grain toast. Cook on a lightly oiled pan, adding the meat first, then pouring in the beaten eggs.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Best enjoyed immediately. If needed, store in a sealed container in the refrigerator for up to 24 hours. Reheat in a pan or microwave to an internal temperature of 75 °C.
